later_review_audit.description: LlamaChat uses Sparkle's SPUStandardUpdaterController and exposes a manual update check. The recovered source does not substantiate an application-pinned Sparkle EdDSA key; key configuration and released artifact verification remain unresolved.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than historical release re-verification; Sparkle runtime enforcement, application metadata, key configuration outside the cited project file, and released artifacts were not independently audited.

original_evidence.text: | LlamaChat | alexrozanski/LlamaChat | Swift/SwiftUI, macOS app, uses the Sparkle framework | Y | Y — `SPUStandardUpdaterController(startingUpdater: true, ...)` starts Sparkle's standard automatic-update lifecycle at launch, in addition to a manual "Check for Updates" action | Y (Sparkle downloads the update and, once verified, installs it — final install still requires the user to accept Sparkle's install prompt per Sparkle's standard UX) | https — `SUFeedURL` = `https://llamachat.app/api/appcast.xml` | Y — Sparkle appcast items are signed; the app embeds the corresponding public key for verification | signature — EdDSA/Ed25519, Sparkle's standard `SUPublicEDKey` scheme | embedded public key in `Info.plist` (`SUPublicEDKey`), not fetched over the network | `LlamaChat/Info.plist`: `SUFeedURL` = `https://llamachat.app/api/appcast.xml`; `SUPublicEDKey` = `kYcF5CTAVZ6ljL01giZNTfMtJCDUl/DUUQ5FsibYCx8=`; `LlamaChat/viewmodel/updates/CheckForUpdatesViewModel.swift:9` (`import Sparkle`); `:14-19` (`updaterController = SPUStandardUpdaterController(startingUpdater: true, updaterDelegate: nil, userDriverDelegate: nil)`; `checkForUpdates()` → `updaterController.updater.checkForUpdates()`) |
